kernel: the prefill and fusion host settings: prefillDqGemm (dequantize the affine weight to a bf16 [N, K] transient and run the dense steel GEMM over stock qmm_t's 32x32x32 dead zone, with the per-shape M5 Ultra NAX floor), the mid-graph eval cadence and its PREFILL_EVAL_MIN_SEQ verify-width exemption, the paid fusion set (fused MoE router top-K, SwiGLU and gelu over a 65536-pattern sigmoid table, add_norm residual+next-norm, the MoE down-path tail gatherQmvDownReduce, the GDN decode fusions), the one-expert expert-bank view binding rule, the small-model row-join and residual-norm fixes, the small dense kernels mxfp8_qmv.metal, ple_gather.metal and hc_prefill_norm/mix.metal, and the MLX_SERVE_DISPATCH_PROBE chain pricing
summary: Serves prefill widths and the decode fusion set on Metal. At M >= 2048 (384 at 2-bit) affine projections dequantize to a bf16 [N, K] transient (per-call cost under 1 ms by their account) and run the steel GEMM instead of stock qmm_t's stalled 32x32x32 tile; on the M5 Ultra's NAX stock qmm is the fused kernel and keeps the call until about 0.9 x min(N, K) rows. Decode fusions ship behind measured chain-shortening gates: the dispatch probe (MLX_SERVE_DISPATCH_PROBE=N) prices a chained dispatch at 1.5 to 1.7 us on an M4 Max and 2.8 us on an M5 Ultra, and only the fusions that shorten the dependency chain paid (router + SwiGLU 2.7% together, down tail 1.5%, GDN decode 3.9% of a Flash Next forward); small dense models got row-joined q|k|v and gate|up, one residual kernel, and 65536-pattern unary activation tables for +4 to +10% decode.

settings.name: prefill_dq_gemm_min_m
settings.condition: affine 3/4/5/6/8-bit: M from which dequant+steel-GEMM takes over from stock qmm_t; decode (M=1) and spec-verify widths never route
settings.note: tuned against stock qmm_t's 32x32x32 steel tile; kill switch MLX_SERVE_PREFILL_DQ_GEMM=0 (comment at src/transformer.zig:43896-43897)

settings.name: prefill_dq_gemm_min_rows_2bit
settings.condition: 2-bit affine only
settings.note: 2-bit qmm loses from 384 rows: M4 Max 5120x17408 +5% at 384, +10% at 1024 (doc comment at src/transformer.zig:43900-43902)

settings.name: prefill_dq_gemm_ultra_floor_fraction
settings.condition: M5 Ultra NAX only, 4/5/6/8-bit, once both N and K are 4096 or more and K < 3N: floor = max(base, 0.9 x min(N, K))
settings.note: there stock qmm is the fused NAX kernel and beats the dequant route below that row count; the M5 Max crosses the other way on K 5120, so only the dual-die arch gets the shape-aware floor (src/transformer.zig:43940-43945)

settings.name: prefill_dq_gemm_ultra_min_dim
settings.condition: min(N, K) below this keeps the base floor on the Ultra (Flash-Next K 640 and 2560, N 2560), and K >= 3N keeps it because the dense GEMM runs MLX's split-K kernel there
settings.note: K 5120 (Qwen3.8-27B) crosses at about 4608 rows, K 6144 at 5120; the test at src/transformer.zig:43920-43938 pins the per-shape floors

settings.name: prefill_dq_gemm_cuda_default_off
settings.condition: MLX_SERVE_PREFILL_DQ_GEMM unset: on Metal the route defaults on, on CUDA off
settings.note: CUDA measured slower than stock qmm (3845 vs 4400 tok/s, Llama 3.2 3B, RTX 5060 Ti) and its bf16 weight transients stacked about 5 GB into the prefill peak (comment at src/transformer.zig:43956-43957)

settings.name: prefill_eval_min_seq
settings.condition: forwards narrower than this skip the mid-loop eval cadence entirely
settings.note: spec-verify widths 2..9 ride the prefill layer loops but their transients are decode-scale, so the periodic eval only drained the pipeline: 16 drains per MTP round on a 64-layer model, depth-1 rounds 48 ms where the AR forward is about 34 ms (comment at src/transformer.zig:20671-20680)

settings.name: prefill_eval_cadence_layers
settings.condition: the prefill layer loop evals at most every N layers (also MOE_EVAL_EVERY_N_LAYERS)
settings.note: one value for the prefill loops and the admission bill: at most cadence + 1 linear layers hold a chunk-wide stream between cadence points

settings.name: prefill_eval_transient_budget
settings.condition: per-layer prefill transient above which the layer loop evals after EVERY layer instead of the default cadence
settings.note: 2 << 30; calibrated live on gemma-4-26B-A4B-qat-4bit (M4 Max): eval-per-layer costs about 4.5% prefill at a 5K prompt and flips on at about 8K tokens, where peak 51.6 -> 27.0 GB buys the margin for a 32 GB Mac

settings.name: dispatch_probe_default_count
settings.condition: MLX_SERVE_DISPATCH_PROBE=N injects N exact 1.0 multiplies per MoE layer inside moeMLP2, chained onto expert_x; 0 or unparsable = off
settings.note: injection at src/transformer.zig:33951-33975: the result feeds the expert path so MLX cannot elide it, which is what makes the slope a price for a dispatch in the live graph

settings.name: swiglu_table_patterns
settings.condition: the fused SwiGLU / gelu / sigmoid arms index a table of MLX's own sigmoid evaluated over every 16-bit pattern of the dtype, bf16 and f16 slots built once at first use
settings.note: all16BitPatterns then mlx_sigmoid, materialized once (src/transformer.zig:41233-41239); 128 KB resident per their comment (src/transformer.zig:41188-41191); an exhaustive sweep found MLX's rounding on exactly one bf16 pattern (-6.84375) that random sampling missed

settings.name: down_reduce_lanes_per_row
settings.value: 8, or 16 on the M5 (device generation 17, non-phone)
settings.condition: the MoE down+reduce kernel's lanes per output row; 32 / LPR rows per simdgroup
settings.note: 16 is measured on G17 (M5); a generation nobody measured keeps 8; the solo and rows kernels share it so a row keeps one accumulation order

settings.name: moe_bank_views_one_expert_default
settings.condition: MLX_SERVE_MOE_BANK_VIEWS unset: the affine-4 MoE decode kernels bind one-expert views of the gate/up/down banks instead of the whole banks
settings.note: MLX bills a command buffer for the data_size of every array a kernel binds and a whole 419 MB bank forced a commit per kernel; the kernels address experts from the buffer pointer, so the view only changes billing (src/moe_affine4.zig:181-183)

settings.name: add_norm_max_rows
settings.condition: the decode-width residual add fused with the next block's norm serves batch * seq <= 16
settings.note: seam default add_norm_max_rows = mamba2_decode.MAX_ROWS (src/transformer.zig:3531); the decode loop gates it with fuse_add_norm = !is_prefill (src/transformer.zig:21844); bit-equal to add then fast::rms_norm per the file header (src/add_norm.zig:15-20)

settings.name: fused_rows_max_m
settings.condition: the loader joins q|k|v and gate|up rows into one buffer with axis-0 views only at decode width M == 1
settings.note: from M == 2 the verify lanes and MLX's split-K pick kernels by N, so the joined matrix would reduce K in another order; load reports [load] row-joined projection groups: N (src/transformer.zig:17900)

settings.name: mxfp8_qmv_max_rows
settings.condition: the MXFP8 qmv kernel serves 1..8 activation rows; wider stays on MLX's matmul
settings.note: rows check at src/mxfp8_qmv.zig:42; the weight row is decoded once per lane and applied to every row of x

settings.name: mxfp8_qmv_device_generations
settings.condition: Apple GPU generations the kernel engages on; other generations and phones keep MLX's kernel
settings.note: their comment: measured on M4 (g16) and the M5 Ultra (g17); e8m0 exponent per 32, e4m3 pair decoded by bit placement

settings.name: hc_prefill_max_seq
settings.condition: hyper-connection prefill norm/mix kernels: seq <= max_seq / batch
settings.note: 8192 + TAIL_MERGE_MAX (512, src/generate.zig:1251) - 1, to include the final remainder the chunker may merge into an 8192-token chunk

settings.name: hc_prefill_min_seq
settings.condition: geometry takes seq > 16 with batch 1..2
settings.note: below it the composed op chain serves the seam

settings.name: hc_prefill_max_hidden
settings.condition: hidden 128..4096 in steps of 128 and 1..8 hyper-connections, bf16 only
settings.note: MLX_SERVE_HC_PREFILL=0 kills both kernels; hc_prefill_norm.metal preserves Apple's rms_single_row four-value reduction and bf16 rounding (file header); the mix kernel reads the same 65536-pattern sigmoid table

settings.name: ple_table_row_bytes
settings.condition: the n-gram embedding table mapping is reshaped to [len / 4096, 4096] as the no-copy GPU buffer ple_gather.metal indexes
settings.note: shape build at src/ple_gpu.zig:117-121; one thread per output element in the kernel, n-gram order 2 + h / params[2] per head

gates.condition: prefillDqGemm admission: enabled (env default on Metal, off CUDA) and bits in {2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8} affine and x bf16/f16 and rows >= prefillDqGemmRowFloorNow(bits, n, k); otherwise the caller stays on stock qmm
prefillDqGemmRowFloor: !ultra_nax or bits == 2 or min(N, K) < 4096 or K >= 3N keeps the base floor; only the M5 Ultra NAX with both N and K >= 4096 and K < 3N raises it to 0.9 x min(N, K)
prefillEvalCadenceApplies(seq_len): the mid-graph eval cadence applies only for seq_len >= PREFILL_EVAL_MIN_SEQ (32), exempting the spec-verify widths that ride the prefill layer loops
dispatch probe: dispatchProbeCount() > 0 chains that many exact 1.0 multiplies onto expert_x inside moeMLP2; the result feeds the expert path so nothing elides it

MoE router fusion (moeRouterTopK, one kernel for top-K + softmax/renormalize incl. the shared-expert gate fold): moeRouterFusedEnabled() (MLX_SERVE_MOE_ROUTER_FUSED != 0) and a GPU stream; every unsupported geometry returns null and callers keep the composed routing chain

SwiGLU and table-multiply fusion arms gate on swigluFusedEnabled() (MLX_SERVE_SWIGLU_FUSED != 0) and a GPU stream and bf16/f16 dtypes, each arm re-checking (for example src/transformer.zig:41610 and src/transformer.zig:41880)

add_norm decode seam: fuse_add_norm = !is_prefill and batch * seq <= add_norm_max_rows (16) and add_norm.eligible (GPU stream, bf16/f16, hidden width the thread layouts cover, src/add_norm.zig:130-136)

fuseRowGroup: 2..4 quantized {w, s, b} triples sharing one packed geometry (same packed width and dtype, same scales width and dtype, same bias presence) joined along axis 0 at FUSED_ROWS_MAX_M == 1, originals rewritten as zero-copy row views
MoE bank views: bindViews returns null unless viewsOn() (MLX_SERVE_MOE_BANK_VIEWS != 0) and every bank carries scales; dense banks keep the whole-array bind

GDN decode fusions (gdnPreworkFused generalized to S 1..9 with in-kernel gate chain and beta, gdnNormGateFused epilogue for the per-head norm and out gate): gdnDecodeFusedEnabled() (MLX_SERVE_GDN_DECODE_FUSED != 0); MLX_SERVE_GDN_PREWORK=0 kills the whole prework kernel

MoE down-path tail (gatherQmvDownReduce: down gather + score multiply + sum in one kernel): downReduceFusedEnabled() (MLX_SERVE_MOE_DOWN_REDUCE_FUSED, src/transformer.zig:43113) and moeRowsFusedEnabled() and not MLX_SERVE_MOE_GATHER_QMV_OFF and hidden_act == .silu and gate/up sharing one (bits, group, mode) and down affine 2/4/8-bit or nvfp4 g16 and N % 4 == 0

hc_prefill norm/mix eligibility: inject present, bf16 across x, weight and inject, enabled (MLX_SERVE_HC_PREFILL), geometry(batch 1..2, seq > 16, seq <= max_seq / batch), hc 1..8, hidden 128..4096 divisible by 128

measured.conditions: MLX_SERVE_DISPATCH_PROBE 0/4/8; slope about 0.067 ms per dispatch-per-layer, i.e. about 1.5-1.7 us per chained GPU dispatch at 40 layers

measured.value: 11.07 / 11.61 / 12.13 ms GPU at N=0/4/8, about 2.8 us per chained op
measured.model: Qwen3.8 Flash-Next, iQ-MLX 4.7 bpw (forward reads 5.9 GB per token against a 5.4 ms bytes floor)
measured.conditions: MLX_SERVE_DECODE_FWD_UBENCH=30; the decode graph has 2056 nodes, about 1180 kernels (579 custom, 315 qmm), 22 per GDN+MoE layer

measured.model: Laguna XS (router arm), gemma4-26B-A4B (softmax router arm), dense Qwen3.6-27B (SwiGLU arm)
measured.conditions: MoE router and SwiGLU fusions together, position-balanced across six pairs in both orders, medians 13.418 -> 13.061 ms/forward; /v1/chat/completions at temp 0 byte-identical over 260 tokens
MoE down-path tail fusion, live paired A/B: 8.58 vs 8.71 and 8.56 vs 8.70 ms/tok (-1.45% / -1.53%), on-arm wins both pairs both orders; greedy 200-token on/off byte-identical

measured.model: Qwen3.8 Flash-Next (qwen4_exp), serial decode, in-situ on the real pack
measured.conditions: GDN decode fusion gdnPreworkFused + gdnNormGateFused (MLX_SERVE_GDN_DECODE_FUSED): 15.45 -> 14.84 ms/forward, serial 60.0 -> 60.4 tok/s short, 52.7/53.4 -> 53.5/54.2 at 8.5k; 179/180 per-layer checks exact, one k element off by 1 bf16 ulp

measured.value: Spark +10, Gemma E4B +9, Gemma MoE +7, LFM2.5 +4
measured.conditions: all fixes bit-identical (q|k|v and gate|up rows joined at load, fusedResidualNorm, unary activations tabulated over all 65536 patterns then one multiply); prefill untouched; the small models decoded at 55-65% of the bandwidth floor while the 27B sat at 88%; a 4B forward was about 940 kernels at about 3 us GPU idle per dependent small kernel
same-session defaults vs defaults against oMLX; the 8k/32k ties are roofline physics, the winnable margins are short contexts and MoE or small models
2 x 27e9 FLOP per token at MLX's measured 14.4 TFLOPS bf16 GEMM rate (89% of the M4 Max's theoretical 16.2) puts the 8k roofline at about 30.9 s and both engines within 3-6% of it

--ane-prefill, ABA-counterbalanced boots vs the same binary without the flag; int8 rows, fp16 datapath, lossy by design, opt-in default off; decode byte-flat, greedy echo byte-identical at 200 tokens; measured a loss on M5 Max (PR #223)

MLX_MAX_OPS_PER_BUFFER=200 with the MB cap lifted, 3+3 boots; the encoder stopped being throttled (3.8 ms) but the GPU started later and the head/tail overlap went; the about 5 us between kicks is not recoverable by packing

measured.model: E-sweep fixture, all reading the same 10 experts
measured.conditions: MLX's gather_qmm at decode width costs in proportion to the expert bank's size, not the work; flat under pip-Python with the identical dylib; 141 gathers/token x 300 us was the whole 42 ms/token Laguna decode

lab_mapping.maps_to: lab evaluator item L1 (docs/MLX_SERVE_KERNELS.md, What the lab should take): tslab profile --dispatch-probe N over {0, 4, 8} fitting us_per_chained_dispatch into the ledger; proposed there, not built: crates/lab/src/knobs.rs has no TURBOSPARK_DISPATCH_PROBE knob today
lab_mapping.note: the probe is pure (no KV writes) and observable (the result feeds the expert path), which is why it beats run-the-component-twice marginal pricing

lab_mapping.maps_to: TURBOSPARK_PREFILL_STEEL (crates/lab/src/knobs.rs knob prefill_steel, families qwen35 and qwen36, KlBounded): our steel prefill route, the surface the dequant+GEMM dead-zone story maps onto

TURBOSPARK_QWEN_FUSED_FFN (crates/lab/src/knobs.rs knob qwen_fused_ffn): our MoE/FFN fusion arm; their rule is that a fusion pays only if it shortens the dependency chain, and a chain the GPU already overlaps is not a dispatch to fuse

none yet for the row-join and residual-norm fusions themselves; the measurement side is lab item L5 (tslab trace over xctrace Metal System Trace) and the engagement-report pattern ([load] row-joined projection groups: N) is what lab item L3 wants every arm to prove

Doc-vs-source: our doc says the ANE split was a loss on both M5 Max testers; the source says only measured a loss on M5 Max, PR #223 (docs/gotchas/engine-mlx.md:3269) and never counts two testers. Our doc's Spark 4B is Spark-X2.5 4B in the source, and the source also lists Gemma 4 26B-A4B among the launch-bound models while the gain line reads Gemma MoE +7%. The under-1-ms dequant transient is the source's own claim (docs/gotchas/engine-mlx.md:284, per-call dequant <1 ms); the pinned code asserts no cost. The doc's 1.5% down-tail figure is the heading number; the source's measured pairs are -1.45% and -1.53%. The doc's three fused GDN decode dispatches figure is the -3.9% forward of gdnPreworkFused + gdnNormGateFused on the qwen4_exp hybrid, not the two-dispatch decode of src/gdn_decode.zig that the separate gdn_decode pinned entry covers. Two distinct residual+norm kernels exist in the source: add_norm.zig fuses a decode residual add with the NEXT block's norm (bit-equal to add then fast::rms_norm), while the small-model fixes use fusedResidualNorm (RESIDUAL_NORM_SOURCE, src/transformer.zig:40733), one kernel doing pre-norm, add, scale and post-norm with MLX's rms_single_row tree; our doc mentions both without separating them. The prefill section's second intervention (a single long msv_attn_p256 dispatch tripping macOS IOGPU preemption, fixed by capping per-dispatch work with fp32 online-softmax state carried between key-range dispatches) is attention-side and left to the attention pinned entries. The command-buffer packing result is a null result: bigger buffers lose (10.82 vs 10.45 ms). Machine and quant for the small-model gains and the GDN fusion percentage are not stated in the source sections quoted here.
